name: Theoretical computer science: Exact XOR-circuit synthesis
description: Exact XOR-circuit synthesis under a bounded candidate interface with independent verification; generated mathematical instances, no external dataset.

sources.locator: Boyar and Peralta: straight-line XOR circuits for linear maps over GF(2).

evaluation.benchmark: Theoretical computer science: Exact XOR-circuit synthesis
evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: synthesize(matrix, depth_limit) -> {'gates': [[wire, wire], ...], 'outputs': [wire,...]}. Input wires are 0..n-1, constant-zero wire is n, gate k (zero-based) produces wire n+1+k. Exact symbolic GF(2) verification; depth <=16. Minimize mean gate-count / independent-row baseline over 8x8,12x16,16x16 binary maps.

limitations: This is a bounded native adaptation, not the paper's experimental score or an asymptotic guarantee.
Public development generators can be inspected; independent generalization requires fresh instances after freezing the candidate.

papers.title: A New Combinational Logic Minimization Technique with Applications to Cryptology
papers.task_relation: The local task isolates XOR straight-line synthesis for generated GF(2) matrices and verifies exact equivalence. It omits nonlinear gates and full cryptographic designs, so it does not establish an AES implementation improvement.
papers.primary_goal: Reduce combinational circuit size, including the gate cost of linear transformations used in cryptographic implementations.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Minimize the number of XOR gates needed to implement a specified binary linear transformation.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Reducing linear-circuit complexity is a central component of the cited circuit-minimization research.
science_relevance.reason: Circuit minimization is a substantive engineering and theoretical-computing target of the source, not merely an example supplied to a generic agent.
